sentences.text:
1. KALE VIJAYA RAJU Counsel for the Respondent/complainant(S):
 1. PUBLIC PROSECUTOR (AP)
ORDER:

The instant Criminal Petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 has been filed, by the Petitioner/Accused No.2, seeking to quash the proceedings against him in C.C.No.720 of 2019 on the file of the Court of Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Allagadda, for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A, 323 read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

entities.text: Court of Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Allagadda
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Heard Sri K.Vijaya Raju, learned counsel for the Petitioner.
Memo filed to the effect that notice has been served on the complainant through the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor before the trial Court.
None represented.
3. Heard Ms.K.Priyanka Lakshmi, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for the respondents.
4. Learned counsel for the Petitioner would submit that the Petitioner herein is Accused No.2 who is the father of Accused No.1.
A false case has been lodged against the Petitioner.
Learned counsel further would submit that nothing is alleged against the Petitioner in the complaint.
The complaint itself would disclose that the marriage of Accused No.1 with respondent No.2 is a love marriage against the wishes of the parents.

Learned counsel further would submit that continuation of the criminal proceedings against the Petitioner is mere abuse of process of law since the Petitioner Katamala Chennakesava Rao vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 5 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150415740/
1 never stayed with Accused No.1 and respondent No.2 at any point of time.

sentences.text: 5. Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor would submit that the Court may pass appropriate orders.

6. Having heard the submissions made by the learned counsel representing both parties and on perusal of the material available on record, the point for determination that arises in this case is as follows:
"Whether the case against the Petitioner /Accused No.2 in C.C.No.720 of 2019 on the file of the Court of Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Allagadda, is liable to be quashed by exercising jurisdiction under Section 482 Cr.P.C."?
Determination by the Court 7.

entities.text: Court of Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Allagadda
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: A bare perusal of Section 482 makes it clear that the Code envisages that inherent powers of the High Court are not limited or affected so as to make orders as may be necessary; (i) to give effect to any order under the Code or, (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any Court or, otherwise (iii) to secure ends of justice.
A court while sitting in Section 482 jurisdiction is not functioning as a court of appeal or a court of revision.

It must exercise its powers to do real and substantial justice,
depending on the facts and circumstances of the case.
These powers must be invoked for compelling reasons of abuse of process of law or glaring injustice, which are against sound principles of criminal jurisprudence.

8. In the context of quashment of criminal proceedings arising out of matrimonial matters, the Hon'ble Apex Court in Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam v. State of Bihar1, held as follows:
"18.

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam v. State of Bihar1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The above-mentioned decisions clearly demonstrate that this court has at numerous instances expressed concern over the misuse of section 498A IPC and the increased tendency of implicating relatives of the husband in matrimonial disputes,
without analysing the long term ramifications of a trial on the complainant as well as the accused.

It is further manifest from the said judgments that false implication by way of general omnibus allegations made in the course of matrimonial dispute, if left unchecked would result in misuse of the process of law.
Therefore, this court by way of its judgments has warned the courts from proceeding against the relatives and in-laws of the husband when no prima facie case is made out against them.

*** * *
22.Therefore, upon consideration of the relevant circumstances and in the absence of any specific role attributed to the accused appellants, it would be unjust if the Appellants are forced to go through the tribulations of a trial, i.e., general and omnibus allegations cannot manifest in a situation where the relatives of the complainant's husband are forced to undergo trial.

It has been 2022 LiveLaw (SC)
141 highlighted by this court in varied instance that a criminal trial leading to an Katamala Chennakesava Rao vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 5 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150415740/
2 eventual acquittal also inflicts severe scars upon the accused, and such an exercise must therefore be discouraged."
(emphasis supplied)
9.

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Achin Gupta v. State of Haryana and another2, highlighted the requirement of taking the realities into consideration and legislating, especially in the context of the Sections 85 and 86 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.

entities.text: Achin Gupta v. State of Haryana and another2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant observations made in the context of the present case highlighting the duty of this Court, in the said judgment is as follows;
"25.

If a person is made to face a criminal trial on some general and sweeping allegations without bringing on record any specific instances of criminal conduct, it is nothing but abuse of the process of the court.

The court owes a duty to subject the allegations levelled in the complaint to a thorough scrutiny to find out, prima facie,
whether there is any grain of truth in the allegations or whether they are made only with the sole object of involving certain individuals in a criminal charge, more particularly when a prosecution arises from a matrimonial dispute."
(emphasis supplied)
10.

Considering the submissions made and on perusal of the material on record and a fair look at the contents of the complaint, as rightly put by learned counsel for the Petitioner there was a love affair between Accused No.1 and respondent No.2 for 2  years preceding to their marriage.
The parents of Accused No.1 did not agree for the marriage.
So their marriage 2024 INSC 369 took place as per the Christian Customs on 28.08.2019.

Except a casual reference in the complaint that since from the marriage at the instance of the Petitioner/Accused No.2 her husband started harassing her mentally and physically for the sake of additional dowry, nothing is attributed against the Petitioner in specific.
Pertinent to note here that the complaint or the material placed on record would not disclose that the Petitioner stayed with Accused No.1 and respondent No.2 for a single day.

In absence of any specific allegations made against the Petitioner, except a casual reference of his name in the complaint, continuation of criminal proceedings against him is a sheer abuse of process of law.

11. In the backdrop of legal position referred supra and in the facts and circumstances of the present case, no prima facie case is made out against the petitioner for the offences punishable under Section 498-A, 323 read with 34 of the IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the D.P.Act.
In that view the criminal petition is liable to be allowed.

12. In the result, the Criminal Petition is allowed by quashing the criminal proceedings against the Petitioner/Accused No.2 in C.C.No.720 of 2019 on the file of the Court of Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Allagadda.
